title: How to hide cursor in PowerPoint on Mac: simple steps for a cleaner presentation
metaTitle: How to hide cursor in PowerPoint on Mac (Step-by-Step)
description: Learn how to hide cursor on Mac while presenting in PowerPoint. Follow our guide to toggle pointer visibility using keyboard shortcuts or menu options.
targetKeyword: how to hide cursor on mac
intro: To hide your cursor during a PowerPoint presentation on a Mac, you can use the keyboard shortcut ⌘ + I. Alternatively, you can right-click anywhere on the screen during your slideshow, navigate to Pointer Options, then Arrow Options, and select Hidden.
tldr: Use ⌘ + I to toggle the cursor on or off while presenting.
Right-click during a slideshow and select Pointer Options > Arrow Options > Hidden.
The Mac version does not support a permanent 'always hidden' setting.
The cursor state resets when you restart the slideshow.

blocks.text: Why hide the cursor during a presentation

Presentations often look cleaner without a distracting mouse pointer moving across the screen. When you use your mouse to navigate, it draws attention away from your content. Keeping the screen clear helps your audience focus on the slides. This is especially true for kiosk displays, church services, or professional decks. Many presenters find that a visible cursor feels informal. Removing it creates a more polished, cinematic feel for your audience.
How to hide cursor on Mac using shortcuts

The fastest way to manage your cursor is the built-in keyboard shortcut. During your slideshow, you do not need to pause or exit your presentation. Simply press ⌘ and the letter I on your keyboard. This command acts as a toggle. If the cursor is visible, it will disappear. If it is hidden, it will reappear. This method works instantly and keeps your flow intact while you speak.

If you prefer using your mouse or trackpad, you can access the same setting through the on-screen menu. Start your slideshow as you normally would. While in full-screen mode, right-click anywhere on the slide. A menu will appear with several options. Look for Pointer Options. From there, select Arrow Options. You will see a submenu where you can choose Hidden. This will remove the cursor until you move the mouse again or toggle it back.

PowerPoint for Mac does not have an 'Always Hidden' setting. On Windows, some users can configure the app to start with the cursor hidden by default. This feature is currently missing on the Mac version. You must manually hide the cursor every time you start a new slideshow session. If you exit the presentation and restart it, the cursor will return to its default visible state.

Another difference involves multi-display setups. On a Mac, the cursor may sometimes duplicate or appear on the wrong monitor when it enters the active slide area. This behavior is specific to how macOS handles window focus. If you notice the cursor appearing unexpectedly, try moving your mouse to a corner of the screen that is not part of the active presentation area.

Sometimes the shortcut ⌘ + I might not work as expected. This usually happens if the cursor is interacting with an active element on the slide. If you have buttons, links, or interactive objects, the app might keep the cursor visible to allow for interaction. Try moving the mouse away from these elements before pressing the shortcut. If the problem persists, check that your keyboard layout is set correctly.

Some users look for workarounds to keep the cursor hidden permanently. While some developers use VBA macros to force this behavior, these are not officially supported by Microsoft. They can lead to stability issues or security warnings. For most users, sticking to the native toggle method is the safest way to maintain a clean presentation without risking app crashes.

If you are using PowerPoint for the web, the experience is different. The web version is a lighter app than the desktop version. It does not support the same advanced presentation settings or VBA macros. Many of the keyboard shortcuts that work in the desktop app are not available in the browser. If you need full control over your cursor and presentation environment, use the desktop version of PowerPoint 365.

faq.question: Can I hide the cursor permanently in PowerPoint on Mac?
faq.answer: No, PowerPoint for Mac does not offer a native setting to keep the cursor hidden permanently. You must hide it each time you start a presentation.

faq.question: Does ⌘ + I work on all versions of PowerPoint for Mac?
faq.answer: Yes, this shortcut is standard for current versions of Microsoft 365 on macOS. If it does not work, ensure your keyboard focus is on the presentation window.

faq.question: Why does my cursor keep reappearing?
faq.answer: The cursor will typically reappear if you move the mouse or trackpad. Ensure your mouse is not resting on the surface where it might move accidentally.

troubleshooting.problem: Shortcut ⌘ + I does not hide the cursor.
troubleshooting.fix: Ensure the presentation window is active and you are not hovering over an interactive element like a button.
Check that your mouse or trackpad is not being bumped. Any movement will cause the cursor to reappear.
